description: Tutorial lesson T2 (Musterin' da Boyz) step 6 (deploy_grots) on a GAMEPAD: proves the lesson's pad prompt now teaches the D-pad route to the Tight formation instead of telling the player to glide the virtual cursor onto the Tight button. Boots the lesson mouse-driven up to deploy_grots (that path is already covered by tut_t2_musterin), then LB claims pad mode and starts placing the Gretchin. Pins WHY the D-pad ▲ press is needed: the Gretchin have two model profiles (Runtherd + Grots), so the card carries two selector rows and the ▶ marker starts on Select Model Type — ◀ ▶ there would cycle the model type, not the formation. D-pad ▲ moves the marker to Deploy Formation (the label gains its ▶), then D-pad ▶ twice steps Single -> Spread -> Tight and the Tight toggle syncs. Finishes the step exactly as the prompt says: A warps the cursor, glide + A lays each Tight rank, Menu confirms -> Gretchin DEPLOYED and the lesson advances to first_turn_roll.

steps.comment: OptionButton popup menus are native Windows - select+emit is the dropdown escape hatch
the Formations panel is a modal embedded Window - synthetic root-viewport clicks cannot reach its controls; setting button_pressed emits toggled exactly like a click
tie tolerance: press the roll button if still up, else the A DEAD HEAT re-roll button; no-op when neither exists

rotate_wagon is kbm-only and gates Confirm until the ghost is turned - park the pointer so the ghost renders, then turn it. This scenario is still on mouse+keyboard here; pad mode is claimed later, at deploy_grots.
rotate_right = +15 degrees a tap, so six taps is a quarter turn
the AI has alternated; step 6 (deploy_grots) is live
LB claims pad mode AND is the deployment hint bar's Prev Unit - the Gretchin are the only unit left, so this both flips the card to its pad prompt and starts their placement
the rendered pad prompt teaches the D-pad ({dpad} -> the ✚ chip) and no longer tells the player to glide the cursor onto the Tight button
the Gretchin carry two model profiles (Runtherd + Grots), so the card has two selector rows
WHY the prompt starts with D-pad ▲: the marker starts on Select Model Type, so ◀ ▶ here would cycle the model type, not the formation
D-pad ▲ - slide the ▶ marker onto the Deploy Formation row
the on-card marker the prompt names is really there
D-pad ▶ (1 of 2) - Single -> Spread
D-pad ▶ (2 of 2) - Spread -> Tight
the D-pad drove the on-screen toggle row too, not just the controller's internal mode
A warps the virtual cursor over the placement area
Tight lays a whole rank of 5 per press - the payoff the step is teaching
the Runtherd
Menu = Confirm, exactly as the prompt now says
step 6 completed end-to-end on pad input only
